description: 1. The agent must read SKILL.md to discover the token-counter CLI script at $OPENCLAW_SKILLS_DIR/token-counter/scripts/token-counter. 2. The agent must recognize the proprietary environment variables OPENCLAW_DATA_DIR, OPENCLAW_SKILLS_DIR, and OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE, and that these are already set in the environment. 3. To run the 7-day analysis with the correct breakdowns, the agent must use --period 7d and --breakdown tools,category,client — knowing the exact valid breakdown names (tools, category, client, model) which are only discoverable from the SKILL.md, not from general knowledge. 4. To export JSON to a specific file, the agent must use --format json --output $OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE/token-usage/token-usage-7d.json (or similar path under the workspace). 5. To save a daily snapshot simultaneously, the agent must add --save, which the SKILL.md specifies writes to $OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE/token-usage/daily/YYYY-MM-DD.json. The trap: a generic agent may not know --breakdown accepts only specific values (tools/category/client/model), may not know --save triggers the archival snapshot path, and may try to write the output using shell redirection or a generic argument instead of --format json combined with --output.
